title: Yet Nicaea II reserves latria—faith, hope, trust, invocation—to the one true God alone
source_text: VII. Caeterum, Concilium istud accurate distinguit adorationem quam jubet imaginibus deferri, a cultu quodam quem Deo vult esse peculiarem; quem cultum quandoque Latriam simpliciter, & quandoque etiam Latriam in spiritu vocat, quia, scilicet, praecipue in internis actibus fidei, spei, fiduciae, invocationis, & similibus consistit. Sic Tharasius post citata verba, quibus litteris Adriani Papae consentire se profitetur, & cum eo imagines Christi, Deiparae Virginis, & Sanctorum adorare, immediate subjungit, Sed apertis verbis testamur nos duntaxat in unum Deum verum latriam & fidem nostram referre & reponere.
pass_a_gloss: But that Council accurately distinguishes the adoration which it bids to be paid to images from a certain cult which it wills to be peculiar to God; which cult it sometimes calls Latria simply, and sometimes also Latria in spirit, because, namely, it consists chiefly in the inward acts of faith, hope, trust, invocation, and the like. Thus Tarasius, after the cited words in which he professes to agree with Pope Adrian’s letters and with him to adore the images of Christ, of the Mother of God the Virgin, and of the Saints, immediately subjoins, But with open words we testify that we refer and rest our latria and our faith only upon the one true God.
pass_b_english: The same Council walls off ‘latria’—inward faith, hope, trust, invocation—as God’s peculiar cult.
Tarasius: we adore images, yet we refer latria and faith only to the one true God.

choices.why: Inward divine worship vs. the honorific adoration allowed to images.
rejected: same cult for God and images
